title: Local Clusters with minikube
summary: Pick a practice environment, start minikube, deploy and expose an app, and use addons.

blocks.text: First install **kubectl**, the command-line tool for talking to a cluster. Then choose a place to experiment:

rows: Kubernetes IN Docker: runs cluster nodes as Docker containers
Runs a local cluster on Linux, macOS or Windows
Runs in the browser with nothing to install
Production-like clusters on multiple machines. Advanced

blocks.text: Start with kind, minikube or a playground. A kubeadm cluster is significantly more complex to set up.

items: A container or VM manager, for example Docker, Podman, QEMU, KVM, Hyper-V, VirtualBox or VMware

blocks.text: minikube is for learning and development. For production clusters, see the Kubernetes production environment docs.

minikube start
minikube status
kubectl get po -A
`minikube start` creates a **single-node** cluster. That one node is both the control plane and a worker. Production clusters usually keep control plane nodes separate.
`minikube status` should show host, kubelet and apiserver as **Running**, and kubeconfig as **Configured**.

# no kubectl installed? minikube can fetch a matching one
minikube kubectl -- get po -A

# open the Kubernetes Dashboard (add --url to just print the URL)
minikube dashboard

kubectl create deployment hello-node --image=<image>
kubectl get deployments
kubectl get pods
kubectl get events
kubectl logs <pod-name>
By default a Pod is only reachable on its internal cluster IP. To reach it from outside, expose it as a **Service**:

kubectl expose deployment hello-node --type=LoadBalancer --port=8080
kubectl get services
minikube service hello-node

items: On cloud providers, a LoadBalancer Service gets an external IP. On minikube, use `minikube service <name>` to open it.
`minikube tunnel` gives LoadBalancer Services a routable IP. Run it in a separate window.
`kubectl port-forward service/<name> <local-port>:<service-port>` is another way to reach a Service.

blocks.text:
minikube addons list
minikube addons enable metrics-server
kubectl get pod,svc -n kube-system
kubectl top pods
minikube addons disable metrics-server
`kubectl top pods` needs the metrics-server addon. If you see `error: Metrics API not available`, wait a moment and try again.

rows: Pause Kubernetes without affecting deployed apps, then resume
Start an additional, separately named cluster
Change the default memory limit (requires a restart)

blocks.text: Clean up the tutorial objects with `kubectl delete service hello-node` and `kubectl delete deployment hello-node`.

flashcards.back: Kubernetes IN Docker. It runs cluster nodes as Docker containers.

flashcards.front: How many nodes does a plain `minikube start` create?
flashcards.back: One. It acts as both control plane and worker.

flashcards.front: minikube's minimum CPU, memory and disk?
flashcards.back: 2+ CPUs, 2 GB free memory, 20 GB free disk.

flashcards.front: What should a healthy `minikube status` show?
flashcards.back: host, kubelet and apiserver: Running; kubeconfig: Configured.

flashcards.front: Run kubectl without installing it separately?
flashcards.back: `minikube kubectl -- <args>` downloads and runs a matching kubectl.

flashcards.front: Get the Dashboard URL without opening a browser?
Open a LoadBalancer Service on minikube?

flashcards.back: Creates a routable IP for LoadBalancer Services. Run it in a separate window.

flashcards.front: Which addon does `kubectl top pods` need on minikube?

flashcards.back: pause: pauses Kubernetes without impacting deployed apps. stop: halts the cluster.

flashcards.front: Delete every minikube cluster at once?

flashcards.back: No. It is for learning and development.

questions.stem: After a plain `minikube start`, what does the cluster look like?

options.text: One node that is both control plane and worker
options.explanation: minikube start creates a single-node cluster where that node plays both roles.

options.text: Three control plane nodes and one worker
options.explanation: That's an HA layout, not minikube's default.

options.text: One control plane node with workers added automatically
options.explanation: No extra nodes are added by default.

options.text: Worker nodes only, with a managed control plane
options.explanation: minikube runs the control plane locally.

questions.stem: Which are minikube's stated minimum requirements? Select 2.

options.explanation: Listed under "What you'll need".
Listed under "What you'll need".
The stated minimum is 2 GB of free memory.
minikube runs locally; it needs a container or VM manager, not a cloud account.

questions.stem: You exposed a Deployment with `--type=LoadBalancer` on minikube. What is the documented way to open it in a browser?

options.explanation: On minikube, the LoadBalancer type is reachable through the minikube service command.
Lists Services and their IPs, but doesn't open the app.

options.text: Wait for the cloud provider to assign an external IP
options.explanation: That's what happens on cloud providers, not on plain minikube.
Opens the Kubernetes Dashboard UI, not your Service.

questions.stem: `kubectl top pods` on minikube prints `error: Metrics API not available`. What's the documented fix?

options.text: Enable the metrics-server addon, then wait and retry
options.explanation: The tutorial enables metrics-server and says to wait and try again if you see that message.
Deleting the cluster doesn't add metrics support.
kube-proxy handles Service networking, not metrics.
Namespaces aren't the issue here.

questions.stem: Which command lists minikube's built-in addons and whether each is enabled?

options.explanation: This lists the supported addons and their status.
Reports host, kubelet and apiserver state, not addons.
Shows system Pods, not the list of available addons.
That lists API resource types.

questions.stem: True or false: minikube is intended for running production clusters.

options.explanation: minikube's docs say it is for learning and development.
For production, see the Kubernetes production environment docs.

questions.stem: Your laptop has no kubectl installed. How can you still query the minikube cluster?

options.explanation: minikube can download the appropriate kubectl version and run it.
Shows component state, not Pods.
Lists addons, not Pods.
minikube can provide kubectl for you.

options.text: A tool that runs Kubernetes clusters using Docker containers as nodes
options.explanation: kind = Kubernetes IN Docker.
kind runs locally.
Not what kind is.

options.text: A container runtime that replaces containerd
options.explanation: kind is a cluster tool, not a runtime.

questions.stem: Which command gives LoadBalancer Services on minikube a routable IP?

options.explanation: Run it in another window; the EXTERNAL-IP column then shows the routable IP.
pause suspends Kubernetes.
cordon marks a node unschedulable.
That enables metrics, not networking.

questions.stem: You want a second, separate minikube cluster alongside the first. What do you use?

options.explanation: The -p flag starts a separately named cluster.
Without -p it starts (or reuses) the default cluster.
Changes the default memory limit; it doesn't create a cluster.
unpause resumes a paused instance.

questions.stem: True or false: By default, a new Pod is reachable from outside the cluster without a Service.

options.explanation: By default the Pod is only accessible by its internal IP within the cluster.
Expose it as a Service to make it reachable from outside.

questions.stem: Which commands remove the hello-node tutorial objects? Select 2.

options.explanation: Removes the Service created by kubectl expose.
Removes the Deployment and its Pods.
hello-node is not an addon.
cordon applies to nodes, not Deployments.
